title: She Wrote Down Every Dish She Washed for a Year
request: Biku's game theory story script, used as it is: 'make a story on this script for youtube video 16:9' (2026-10-20).
sources: Michael Ross and Fiore Sicoly, "Egocentric Biases in Availability and Attribution", Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, volume 37, issue 3, pages 322 to 336, 1979. Among five experiments, 37 married couples separately rated each spouse's share of everyday jobs (from making breakfast to causing arguments); each person recalled more of their own contributions and claimed more of the credit than their partner gave them, so the two self-estimates typically added up to more than the whole. In pilot tests with percentages, couples remembered and compared their answers afterwards and it caused friction, so the final study had them mark a line instead. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.37.3.322
Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow, 2011. Retells the study: the self-assessed shares added up to more than 100 percent.
Checked by Claude on 2026-10-20 against reports of the paper. What the story invents: the couple, the notebooks, the 4,212 dishes, the boiler and the shirts.
